script.text: Trump says oil just fell almost ten dollars. Is peace with Iran closer?

Trump told Axios on Monday there is no rush to decide on new strikes on Iran. He said, quote, one way or the other, we will do something. He also says oil has dropped almost ten dollars a barrel, which he credits to expectations of no war.

Vice President Vance says he and Trump feel pretty good about reaching a settlement, but warns military options remain. Qatar says both sides are reviewing the mediators' proposals, and differences remain.

Iran says that is not enough. A foreign ministry spokesman says everything depends on Washington accepting Tehran's demands, including an end to the U.S. naval blockade. Iran's foreign minister says Hormuz could reopen within two days if that happens.
Will the Strait of Hormuz reopen this month? Yes or no?

upload.title: Trump: 'No Rush' on Iran, Oil Falls. Peace Closer? #shorts
upload.description:
President Donald Trump told Axios on Monday, November 2, that there is "no rush" to decide whether to resume strikes on Iran, saying: "One way or the other, we will do something." Trump also said oil prices have dropped by almost ten dollars a barrel, which he credits to expectations that there will be no war with Iran. This is Trump's own claim. Vice President JD Vance said he and Trump "feel pretty good about the prospect of reaching a settlement," while warning that military options remain, according to Fox News. Qatar's foreign ministry said both sides are reviewing proposals from the mediators and that differences remain. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said no final agreement can be reached, and the Strait of Hormuz cannot be reopened, unless the U.S. naval blockade ends and Iran's demands are respected. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said Hormuz could reopen within two days under an agreement. Most details come from officials and the parties themselves and could not be independently verified.
